'''Terrence Alexander Jones''' (born January 9, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]].

==High school career==
Jones was ranked the No. 8 player in the class of 2010 by [[Scout.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=3763614 |title=Terrence Jones – Scout Hoops |work=Scout.com |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> the No. 9 player in the [[ESPNU]] 100,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/63851/terrence-jones |title=Terrence Jones – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles |work=ESPN.com |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> and the No. 13 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name=rivals>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Terrence-Jones-76118 |title=TERRENCE JONES |work=Yahoo.com |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> Jones led [[Jefferson High School (Portland, Oregon)|Jefferson High School]] to three straight Oregon class 5A state championships between his sophomore and senior years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kgw.com/story/local/2014/11/25/11693896/ |title=Jefferson three-peats with win over Mountain View |work=KGW.com |date=March 14, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712204420/http://www.kgw.com/story/local/2014/11/25/11693896/ |archive-date=July 12, 2015 }}</ref> As a junior in 2008–09, he averaged 32 points, 13 rebounds, five assists, three blocks and three steals per game. As a senior in 2009–10, he averaged 30 points, 14 rebounds and 6 assists per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite web |url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jones_terrence00.html |title=Terrence Jones Bio |work=ukathletics.com |access-date=November 25, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713025950/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jones_terrence00.html |archive-date=July 13, 2015 }}</ref>

On January 20, 2010, he was named in the Junior National Select Team to compete in the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]], on April 10.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ceglinsky |first=Sean |url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else/ |title=It's the USA Against Everyone Else |work=SlamOnline.com |date=January 20, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> He was also selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kptv.com/story/14779863/jeffersons-terrence-jones-named-all-american-2-12-2010 |title=Jefferson's Terrence Jones Named All-American |work=KPTV.com |date=February 12, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> and the 2010 Jordan Brand Classic.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010jbc.html |title=Jordan Brand Classic |publisher=Nike.com |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=August 26, 2010 |archive-date=September 1, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100901111550/http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010jbc.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Jones committed to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] on April 30, 2010, but did not sign a [[National Letter of Intent]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Allen |first=Percy |url=http://seattletimes.com/html/huskies/2011749015_umen01.html |title=Terrence Ross signs with Huskies; Terrence Jones commits but doesn't sign |work=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 30, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> He ended up changing his mind and on May 19, 2010, he signed a financial aid agreement with [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] instead of a letter of intent.<ref>{{cite web |last=Daschel | first=Nick |url=http://highschoolsports.oregonlive.com/news/article/5440206792650152273/terrence-jones-signs-agreement-with-kentucky/ |title=Terrence Jones signs agreement with Kentucky |work=OregonLive.com |date=May 19, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/11635/report-terrence-jones-signs-with-kentucky |title=Report: Terrence Jones signs with Kentucky |work=ESPN.com |date=May 20, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
Jones had 25 points and 12 rebounds in his debut with Kentucky in a win vs. East Tennessee State. Jones and [[Doron Lamb]] became the first freshman duo in UK history to score 20 points in a debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303160096 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915041950/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=303160096 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 15, 2016 |title=Kentucky wakes up in second half, finishes off ETSU |work=ESPN.com |date=November 12, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref>

On January 11, 2011, Jones came off the bench for the first time in 2010–11 after not being able to participate in that day's practice due to illness. That night, he broke the UK freshman single-game scoring record, putting up 35 points on 11-of-17 shooting against Auburn University. This came just one month after teammate Doron Lamb set the record with 32 points.<ref name="bio" /> The Wildcats advanced to the 2011 Final Four but ended up losing by one point to the University of Connecticut. Jones and Lamb decided to stay a second year at Kentucky instead of enter the NBA draft with freshmen [[Brandon Knight (basketball)|Brandon Knight]], [[Enes Kanter]], junior [[DeAndre Liggins]], and senior [[Josh Harrellson]]. As a freshman, he averaged 15.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.9 blocks per game.<ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/terrence-jones-1.html|title=Terrence Jones|access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref>

Entering his [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|sophomore year]], Jones was part of what was considered one of "the most highly anticipated" Kentucky basketball teams of all time based on pre-season hype, recruit expectations, and existing talent.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nationofblue.com/2011/05/Terrence-Jones-Spurns-the-Cash-Stays-at-Kentucky/ |title=Terrence Jones Spurns the Cash, Stays at Kentucky |work=NationOfBlue.com |date=May 7, 2011 |access-date=November 25, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141125193947/http://www.nationofblue.com/2011/05/Terrence-Jones-Spurns-the-Cash-Stays-at-Kentucky/ |archive-date=November 25, 2014 }}</ref> On October 26, 2011, Jones participated in Kentucky's annual Blue vs. White scrimmage, scoring a school-record 52 points.<ref>{{cite web |last=McCarthy |first=Matt |url=http://kentuckysports.co/terrence-jones-shines-in-blue-white-scrimmage-2/ |title=Terrence Jones Shines In Blue White Scrimmage |publisher=KentuckySports.co |date=October 27, 2011 |access-date=November 25, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141125194014/http://kentuckysports.co/terrence-jones-shines-in-blue-white-scrimmage-2/ |archive-date=November 25, 2014 }}</ref> In 2011–12, he averaged 12.3 points and 7.2 rebounds in 38 game (34 starts).<ref name="stats" /> In the NCAA tournament that season, Jones helped Kentucky win their eighth national championship.

In April 2012, Jones was one of six Wildcats to enter the NBA draft, along with [[Anthony Davis]], [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]], [[Marquis Teague]], [[Doron Lamb]], and [[Darius Miller]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7825727/kentucky-wildcats-starting-five-declares-nba-draft|title=UK's starting five opts for draft|date=April 18, 2012|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 30, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2012/04/16/report-anthony-davis-marquis-teague-terrence-jones-to-declare-for-nba-draft/|title=Report: Anthony Davis, Marquis Teague, Terrence Jones to declare for NBA draft|first=Daniel|last=Martin|date=April 16, 2012|access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> All six players were drafted, setting a record for most players from one school drafted in the NBA draft.

==Professional career==
===Houston Rockets (2012–2016)===
[[File:Terrence Jones.jpg|thumb|left|Jones with the Rockets in October 2012]]
Jones was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |title=NBA Development League: 2012–13 NBA Assignments |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |archive-date=March 27, 2014 }}</ref> On February 4, 2013, Jones was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812091051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=August 12, 2016 }}</ref> However, he was replaced by [[Chris Wright (basketball, born 1989)|Chris Wright]] because he was later recalled by the Rockets and thus was not an "active" player on a D-League roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/all_star_replacements_named_2013_02_14.html |title=Two Replacements Named for the 2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610060233/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/all_star_replacements_named_2013_02_14.html |archive-date=June 10, 2016 }}</ref>

On January 18, 2014, Jones scored a career-high 36 points, along with 11 rebounds and 2 blocks, in a 114–104 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He became the second youngest Rocket to score 30 points or more behind [[Hakeem Olajuwon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140118/MILHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Bucks at Rockets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref>

After playing the first four games of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]], Jones went on to miss the next 41 games due to nerve inflammation in his left leg.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/Rockets-Jones-hopes-to-return-against-Mavs-6044279.php|title=Rockets' Jones hopes to return against Mavs|date=January 28, 2015 |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on January 28, 2015, against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150128/DALHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Mavericks at Rockets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> On February 27, 2015, he scored a season-high 26 points in a 102–98 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150227/BKNHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Nets at Rockets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> He later missed six games in late March with a partially collapsed lung.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/SACHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Kings at Rockets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref>

Jones again had an injury plagued season in 2015–16, going out in the preseason with a concussion and during the season with a lacerated eyelid and stitches that scratched his eye. Then on February 3, 2016, Jones crashed into another vehicle on his way to the Rockets' flight to Phoenix, remained in the hospital for two days of tests, and was out for the remaining three games before the All-Star break.<ref name=accident>{{cite web|url=http://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/Recovery-from-accident-gives-Rockets-Jones-6845773.php|title=Recovery from accident gives Rockets' Jones reason to be grateful|date=February 22, 2016 |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on February 23, but lasted just four games before being deactivated indefinitely on March 2 due to a respiratory illness. On the court, Jones began the season as the starter at power forward with Donatas Motiejūnas out injured. But after 11 games, he was replaced in the starting lineup by [[Clint Capela]].<ref name="accident" />

===New Orleans Pelicans (2016–2017)===
On July 22, 2016, Jones signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-free-agent-forward-terrence-jones|title=Pelicans Sign Free Agent Forward Terrence Jones|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2016|access-date=July 22, 2016}}</ref> On November 16, 2016, he scored a then season-high 26 points while starting in place of the injured [[Anthony Davis]] in an 89–82 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899609|title=Ibaka, Vucevic help Magic beat Pelicans 89–82|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref> On January 23, 2017, he tied his career high with 36 points in a 124–122 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900092|title=Jones, Holiday lead Pelicans past Cavs 124–122|work=ESPN.com|date=January 23, 2017|access-date=January 24, 2017}}</ref> On February 23, 2017, he was waived by the Pelicans following the team's acquisition of [[DeMarcus Cousins]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-waive-terrence-jones|title=Pelicans Waive Terrence Jones|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2017)===
On March 4, 2017, Jones signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-terrence-jones|title=Bucks Sign Terrence Jones|work=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2017}}</ref> He appeared in just three games for the Bucks before being waived by the team on April 1, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-request-waivers-terrence-jones|title=BUCKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON TERRENCE JONES|work=NBA.com|date=April 1, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017}}</ref>

===Qingdao Eagles (2017)===
[[File:青岛国信双星球员特伦斯·琼斯.jpg|thumb|Jones with Qingdao in November 2017]]
On August 1, 2017, Jones signed with the [[Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}} After getting kicked out of practice following a confrontation with the head coach, Jones was released by Qingdao in late November.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/asia/china/254838/terrence-jones-expected-to-leave-qingdao-eagles.html|title=Terrence Jones expected to leave Qingdao Eagles|work=Sportando.com|date=November 22, 2017|access-date=November 25, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/asia/china/255130/qingdao-reportedly-signed-maciej-lampe-to-replace-terrence-jones.html|title=Qingdao reportedly signed Maciej Lampe to replace Terrence Jones|work=Sportando.com|date=November 24, 2017|access-date=November 25, 2017}}</ref> In nine games, he averaged 22.3 points, 11.2 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.3 blocks per game.

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2017–2018)===
On December 18, 2017, Jones was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Acquire Forward Terrance Jones|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-acquire-forward-terrance-jones/|access-date=December 24, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Erie BayHawks (2018–2019)===
For the 2018–19 season, Jones signed with the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hartman |first1=Billy |title=Erie BayHawks Finalize 2018 Training Camp Roster |url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-finalize-2018-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 3, 2018 |date=October 20, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Houston Rockets (2019)===
On February 22, 2019, Jones signed a 10-day contract with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rockets Sign Two Players|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-two-players|access-date=February 22, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2019}}</ref> On March 4, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-re-sign-Terrence-Jones-to-10-day-contract-13661750.php|title=Rockets re-sign Terrence Jones to 10-day contract|work=chron.com|date=March 4, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2019}}</ref> On March 6, he spent a day with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]] on assignment.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ali|first=Salman|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/06/rockets-assign-terrence-jones-to-rockets-g-league-team/|title=Rockets assign Terrence Jones to Rockets' G League Team|work=rocketswire.usatoday.com|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=March 29, 2019}}</ref> Upon the expiration of his second 10-day contract, he was not signed for the rest of the season by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Luke|last1=Adams|title=Rockets Not Re-Signing Terrence Jones|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2019/03/rockets-not-re-signing-terrence-jones.html|date=March 14, 2019|website=hoopsrumors.com|access-date=March 14, 2019}}</ref>

===TNT KaTropa (2019)===
In May 2019, Jones signed with the [[TNT KaTropa]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as the team's import for the [[2019 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-katropa-taps-former-houston-rocket-terrence-jones-for-commissioners-cup-a793-20190505 |title=TNT Katropa taps former NBA player Terrence Jones for Commissioner's Cup |date=May 5, 2019 |publisher=Spin.ph}}</ref> In his PBA debut for the TNT Katropa, Jones recorded 41 points, 14 rebounds and 4 assists in almost 37 minutes of playing time in a win over the NLEX Road Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/sports/05/22/19/pba-ex-rocket-terrence-jones-explodes-for-41-points-to-lead-tnt-past-nlex|title=Ex Rocket Terrence Jones explodes for 41 points to lead TNT past NLEX|publisher=ABS-CBN News|date=May 22, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> In his next game, Jones fuels the TNT with 43 points, 22 rebounds, 5 assists, 3 steals and 5 threes in a win over the Alaska Aces.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/terrence-jones-tnt-katropa-vs-alaska-pba-commissioner-s-cup-a795-20190525|title=Jones breaches 40-point mark again as TNT rips Alaska for second win in row|publisher=SPIN.ph|date=May 25, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> His 43 points and 22 rebounds were his career-highs for any league that he has played, including the NBA. A week later, Jones recorded yet another 40-point game, this time against the Phoenix Fuelmasters. Jones recorded 40 points, 10 rebounds, 6 assists and 4 steals in a 114–88 blowout win against the Fuelmasters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/terrence-jones-40-points-tnt-katropa-vs-phoenix-pba-commissioners-cup-a795-20190602|title=Terrence Jones fires third 40-point effort as TNT blasts Phoenix in heated game|publisher=Spin.ph|date=June 2, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> In this game, Jones and Phoenix Fuelmasters forward [[Calvin Abueva]] were involved in an on-court altercation that nearly led to a full-scale brawl between two sides. Abueva was ejected for the rest of the game for he ignited the altercation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2019/06/05/ex-nba-player-terrence-jones-clotheslined-low-blow-philippines/1350139001/|title=Ex-NBA player Terrence Jones clotheslined after low blow|publisher=USA Today|date=June 2, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> Ten days after the incident, Jones and the TNT Katropa were up against the PBA defending champs, the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel|Barangay Ginebra]]. However, Jones and his team rallied easily against the defending champs. Jones recorded a monster statline of 17 points, 14 rebounds, 16 assists and 6 blocks for the Katropa. It was his first professional career triple-double.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/terrence-jones-has-triple-double-in-tnt-win-over-ginebra-a795-20190612|title=Terrence Jones triple-double shows he can do a lot more than score|publisher=spin.ph|date=June 12, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> Jones joins fellow imports, [[Justin Brownlee]] and [[Allen Durham]] as the only PBA imports to rack up a triple-double in a PBA game in the past decade. The following game, Jones recorded a career-high 49 points to go along with 18 rebounds and 4 assists in a dominating win over the [[Meralco Bolts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/sports/06/15/19/pba-terrence-jones-explodes-for-49-points-as-tnt-routs-meralco|title=Terrence Jones explodes for 49 points, as TNT routs Meralco|publisher=ABS-CBN News|date=June 15, 2019|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> In the following game, Jones had another monster game as he recorded 39 points, 17 rebounds, 6 assists and 7 blocks in almost 47 minutes of playing time against the Columbian Dyip.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-katropa-vs-columbian-dyip-pba-commissioner-s-cup-terrence-jones-a795-20190621|title=Jones, Castro form one-two punch as TNT downs Columbian to regain top spot|publisher=SPIN.ph|date=June 21, 2019|access-date=July 20, 2019}}</ref> On July 3, Jones recorded his second triple-double of the conference after having recorded 33 points, 21 rebounds and 13 assists in a 102–81 win over the Rain Or Shine Elasto Painters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tnt-banks-on-terrence-jones-triple-double-to-put-away-rain-or-shine-a795-20190703|title=TNT banks on Terrence Jones triple-double to put away Rain Or Shine|publisher=SPIN.ph|date=July 3, 2019|access-date=July 20, 2019}}</ref> On July 7, Jones recorded another triple-double as he racked up 36 points, 16 rebounds and 14 assists in a 115–97 win over the Blackwater Elite.<ref>{{cite web|last=Terrado|first=Reuben|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/terence-jones-triple-double-tnt-katropa-blackwater-pba-commissioner-s-cup-a795-20190707|title=Terrence Jones posts triple-double again as hot-shooting TNT rips Blackwater in PBA Commissioners' Cup|publisher=SPIN.ph|date=July 7, 2019|access-date=August 9, 2019}}</ref> After nine days, TNT played their last elimination game against the Purefoods Star Hotshots. Jones almost recorded his third straight triple-double, ending the game with 26 points, 13 rebounds and 8 assists in a 98–83 win over the Hotshots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-07-17/Talk-N-Text-Tropang-Texters-at-Purefoods-Star-Hotshots/334900|title=Talk N Text Tropang Texters 98 at Rain or Shine Elasto Painters 83|date=July 17, 2019|access-date=August 11, 2019}}</ref>

On August 11, 2019, Terrence Jones was crowned as the PBA's best import of the conference, dethroning [[Justin Brownlee]] of the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.abs-cbn.com/pba/news/2019/08/11/pba-terrence-jones-dominates-wins-best-import-59848|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811114032/https://sports.abs-cbn.com/pba/news/2019/08/11/pba-terrence-jones-dominates-wins-best-import-59848|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 11, 2019|title=Terrence Jones dominates and wins Best Import|last=Lintag|first=Paul|publisher=ABS-CBN Sports|date=August 11, 2019|access-date=August 11, 2019}}</ref>

===Mets de Guaynabo (2020)===
On October 21, 2020, it was reported that [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] had added Jones to their roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=19182|title=Terrence Jones dominates and wins Best Import|language=ES|date=October 21, 2020|website=bsnpr.com|access-date=October 21, 2020}}</ref>

On January 14, 2022, Jones signed with [[Yulon Luxgen Dinos]] of the [[Super Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cherkasov |first1=Sergey |title=Terrence Jones (ex Prometey) is a newcomer at Yulon Luxgen |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Ukraine/news/726630/Terrence-Jones-(ex-Prometey)-is-a-newcomer-at-Yulon-Luxgen |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 14, 2022 |date=January 14, 2022}}</ref>

===Grand Rapids Gold (2022)===
On March 3, 2022, Jones was acquired via available player pool by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 3, 2022}}</ref>

===Cariduros de Fajardo (2022)===
On May 9, 2022, Jones signed with [[Cariduros de Fajardo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). On July 12, 2022, Jones scored a career-high 49 points against the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] in the 2022 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]]'s quarterfinals.<ref>[https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/terrence-jones-estalla-con-49-puntos-y-los-cariduros-empatan-la-serie-contra-los-leones/ Jones 49 Points (BSN)]</ref>

===Kaohsiung Steelers (2022)===
On October 28, 2022, Jones joined the [[Kaohsiung Steelers]] of [[Taiwan]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://focustaiwan.tw/sports/202210280010 | title=Former NBA player Terrence Jones joins the Kaohsiung Steelers – Focus Taiwan | date=October 28, 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/sport/archives/2022/10/29/2003787915 | title=Former NBA player Terrence Jones joins Kaohsiung – Taipei Times | date=October 29, 2022 }}</ref>

===Leones de Ponce (2023)===
On April 10, 2023, Jones was signed by the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) as an injury replacement for their import player [[Eric Paschall]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/1993265/ | title=Former Rockets player Terrence Jones signed with Puerto Rican team Leones de Ponce for the 2023 seas… | date=April 10, 2023 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones is cousins with fellow former NBA players [[Damon Stoudamire|Damon]] and [[Salim Stoudamire]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Lawlor|first=Christopher|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4525076 |title=Basketball is in Jones' DNA |work=ESPN.com |date=October 2, 2009|access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref>

In July 2013, Jones was arrested for allegedly stomping on a homeless man who was sleeping outside a nightclub in Portland, Oregon. He was charged with [[harassment]], a Class B misdemeanor, and [[Recognizance|released on his own recognizance]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/9525784/cops-say-terrence-jones-houston-rockets-injured-homeless-man|title=Cops: Rockets' Jones injured homeless man|date=July 31, 2013 |access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pamplinmedia.com/pt/9-news/158024-nba-power-forward-jones-arrested-for-stomping-homeless-mans-legs|title=NBA power forward Jones arrested for stomping homeless man's legs|access-date=September 5, 2016|archive-date=October 27, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221027105822/https://pamplinmedia.com/pt/9-news/158024-nba-power-forward-jones-arrested-for-stomping-homeless-mans-legs|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Jones has a son with a Filipino woman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/fiba/sbp-convincing-terrence-jones-to-have-fil-am-son-secure-a-ph-passport-a2437-20190718|title=SBP moving to secure PH passport for Terrence Jones' Fil-Am son|website=Spin.ph|language=en|access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref>
